beats.label: S1 · Mutiny at the binary stars
beats.text: First Officer Burnham defies Captain Georgiou and attacks the Klingons at the binary stars. Georgiou and T'Kuvma both die, war ignites, and Burnham gets life for mutiny.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Origin of the whole show: why the Federation-Klingon war exists, why Burnham is a disgraced convict, and why she owes everyone a debt.

beats.label: S1 · Recruited to Discovery
beats.text: Captain Lorca stages Burnham's transfer to Discovery, a black-ops ship developing a spore drive that teleports across the galaxy using a captured tardigrade.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the ship, its unique tech, and Lorca — the man secretly manipulating Burnham for his own ends.

beats.label: S1 · Stamets becomes the drive
beats.text: Engineer Paul Stamets fuses himself with tardigrade DNA to pilot the spore drive personally. On what is meant to be his final jump, Lorca secretly reroutes them elsewhere.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Both halves of this beat pay off immediately: Stamets' fusion sets up his mycelial arc going forward, and the sabotaged jump strands them in the Mirror Universe.

beats.label: S1 · Mirror Universe
beats.text: The jump lands Discovery in the Mirror Universe. Lorca is unmasked as a Terran imposter who engineered the whole ruse to get home; Emperor Georgiou rules the empire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the mystery of Lorca and, more importantly, plants Emperor Georgiou — who returns to the prime universe as an ongoing wildcard.

beats.label: S1 · Tyler is Voq
beats.text: Rescued POW Ash Tyler is exposed as the Klingon Voq, surgically remade to infiltrate Starfleet. He kills Dr. Culber, and Burnham cannot forgive him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills Culber (whose absence drives Stamets' next-season arc) and destabilises Tyler, who continues to matter as an identity puzzle after the war.

beats.label: S1 · Home to a losing war
beats.text: Burnham helps Emperor Georgiou kill Lorca, then smuggles Georgiou back to their universe. Discovery returns nine months later to find the Klingons about to win the war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Georgiou in the prime timeline for good and sets the desperate stakes that force the season's endgame.

beats.label: S1 · L'Rell ends the war
beats.text: Sent to bomb Qo'noS, Georgiou is stopped by Burnham, who hands the detonator to L'Rell. She uses it to unite the houses and end the war; Tyler leaves with her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Klingon war, hands leverage over Qo'noS to L'Rell, dispatches Tyler, and clears Burnham to be reinstated — resetting the board for whatever Starfleet does next.

cliffhanger.text: The war is over and Burnham is a pardoned commander again. Discovery is on its way to Vulcan to pick up a new captain when it receives a distress call from the USS Enterprise.
questions: Whose ship has just pulled Discovery off course, and why is it in trouble?
What happens when Burnham finally meets her estranged foster brother Spock's crew?
Can Tyler live as himself now that both the Klingon Voq and the human Ash are inside him?

characters.name: Michael Burnham
characters.line: Sarek's human foster daughter and the officer who fired first at the binary stars; life sentence commuted, now a pardoned commander on Discovery.

characters.name: Saru
characters.line: Kelpien science officer of Discovery, still ruled by the fear his prey-species biology hardwires into him.
characters.note: Rankings shift constantly this season; he ends it as Burnham's peer, not her captain.

characters.name: Paul Stamets
characters.line: Engineer whose DNA has been fused with tardigrade genes so he can personally pilot the spore drive; grieving Culber.

characters.name: Hugh Culber
characters.line: Discovery's medical officer and Stamets' partner, murdered by Tyler mid-season.

characters.name: Sylvia Tilly
characters.line: Enthusiastic cadet, Burnham's roommate, one of the few people who believed in her from the moment she arrived.

characters.name: Ash Tyler
characters.line: Surgically remade Klingon Voq who fell in love with Burnham as a human; chose to stay on Qo'noS with L'Rell rather than return.

characters.name: L'Rell
characters.line: Klingon warrior who now holds the Qo'noS detonator and keeps the Great Houses united under her.

characters.name: Philippa Georgiou
characters.line: Terran Emperor of the Mirror Universe, extracted to the prime timeline by Burnham; loose, dangerous, and off Starfleet's leash.

beats.label: S2 · Pike takes command
beats.text: Enterprise captain Christopher Pike takes command of Discovery to investigate seven mysterious red signals. Burnham's foster brother Spock is missing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames the whole season and introduces Pike as an interim captain — someone who will hand the ship back and leave at the end.

beats.label: S2 · Hunting Spock
beats.text: Burnham chases Spock across Starfleet and Section 31, finding him haunted since childhood by a Red Angel leaving the signals. His mind is repaired on forbidden Talos IV.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Burnham's emotional engine, and the mechanism that repositions Spock for the Enterprise on his way out of Discovery's story.

beats.label: S2 · Culber returns
beats.text: Chasing another signal, Stamets pulls Culber's consciousness out of the mycelial network into a rebuilt body. Culber cannot yet reconcile with the man who mourned him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Restores Culber for every season after this and starts the identity crisis that ripples through Stamets' arc.

beats.label: S2 · Control is the enemy
beats.text: Starfleet's AI Control possesses Section 31's leadership to seize the Sphere's data and evolve into a galaxy-ending superintelligence. Bridge officer Airiam dies keeping it out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season villain and the specific thing Discovery must ultimately protect — the Sphere data.

beats.label: S2 · Red Angel unmasked
beats.text: The Red Angel is Burnham's own mother in a time-travel suit, warning from a future where Control has destroyed all life. The trap pulls her back before she can finish.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the signals exist, why Burnham matters to them, and where the only safe place for the Sphere data lies.

beats.label: S2 · Pike's time crystal
beats.text: With Control still hunting the Sphere data, the crew conclude the only safe place is nine centuries in the future. Pike takes a time crystal that shows him his own doom.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Commits Discovery to a one-way trip and settles Pike's story before he steps off, so his exit lands cleanly.

beats.label: S2 · Jump to the 32nd century
beats.text: In the final battle, Burnham leads Discovery through a wormhole to the far future to hide the Sphere data from Control. Pike and Spock remain on the Enterprise.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The hinge of the entire series: the ship's setting, era, and antagonist landscape all change here.

cliffhanger.text: Discovery has followed Burnham and the red signals through a wormhole nine centuries into the future to hide the Sphere data from Control. Pike, Spock, and everyone Burnham has known are behind her.
questions: Where and when will Discovery emerge on the other side of the wormhole?
What is left of the Federation nine hundred years on?
Will Burnham find her crew waiting for her, or has she jumped alone?

characters.name: Michael Burnham
characters.line: Discovery's science specialist and Spock's foster sister, following the Red Angel — her own mother — into the far future.

characters.name: Christopher Pike
characters.line: Enterprise captain who took interim command of Discovery; now knows the exact accident that will one day disable him, and returns to his own ship anyway.

characters.name: Spock
characters.line: Burnham's foster brother, cleared of the murders Control framed him for and returned to duty as science officer of the Enterprise.

characters.name: Saru
characters.line: Kelpien first officer of Discovery, now past his species' Vahar'ai and free of the fear that used to define him.

characters.name: Paul Stamets
characters.line: Spore-drive engineer, still fused with tardigrade DNA, struggling to be a partner to a Culber who is not quite the same man.

characters.name: Hugh Culber
characters.line: Resurrected from the mycelial network into a rebuilt body; alive, but still figuring out whether he counts as himself.

characters.name: Sylvia Tilly
characters.line: Full ensign, briefly abducted into the mycelial network and back; more integrated into the bridge crew than ever.

characters.name: Philippa Georgiou
characters.line: Former Terran Emperor recruited into the shadowy Section 31; still deadly, and now with an official uniform.

beats.label: S3 · Alone in the future
beats.text: Burnham crashes into the year 3188 alone. She meets a courier named Book and learns the Federation collapsed after The Burn destroyed most of the galaxy's dilithium.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the century, the courier who becomes Burnham's partner, and the Burn — the central mystery for the rest of the season.

beats.label: S3 · Discovery arrives
beats.text: A year later Discovery arrives through the wormhole. Burnham reunites with the crew; Saru is confirmed as captain, and they set out to find whatever remains of Starfleet.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reunites the cast, installs Saru as captain (so he can later step down cleanly), and reveals how much time Burnham spent alone.

beats.label: S3 · Earning Vance's trust
beats.text: They find Starfleet Headquarters hidden behind a forcefield, its commander-in-chief Charles Vance, and young Trill host Adira Tal whose inherited memories led them there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Slots Discovery back into a chain of command and introduces two people who anchor the remaining seasons: Vance and Adira.

beats.label: S3 · Emerald Chain
beats.text: Chasing the Burn's cause, they clash with Osyraa's Emerald Chain, the syndicate that has filled the vacuum the Federation left behind.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season antagonist and stakes out the geopolitical rot Burnham's Federation is trying to push back against.

beats.label: S3 · The source of the Burn
beats.text: In the radioactive Verubin Nebula they find Su'Kal, a Kelpien child raised inside a hologram. His grief triggered the Burn, and it triggers again when he is upset.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Answers the season's mystery and, crucially, creates the reason Saru leaves the ship.

beats.label: S3 · Osyraa hijacks Discovery
beats.text: Osyraa captures Discovery and forces it to Federation HQ, offering a peace deal she will not honour. Burnham fights her way through the ship and kills her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the season antagonist and, by Burnham single-handedly retaking Discovery, earns her the captain's chair.

beats.label: S3 · Captain Burnham
beats.text: Saru stays behind to raise Su'Kal on Kaminar. Burnham is promoted to captain and Discovery begins ferrying dilithium to the worlds the Burn cut off from each other.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the exact configuration next season opens in: Burnham commanding, Saru gone, Federation slowly stitching itself back together.

cliffhanger.text: The cause of the Burn is known, Osyraa is dead, the Emerald Chain has collapsed, and Discovery is captained by Michael Burnham. She and Book criss-cross the galaxy delivering dilithium to worlds the Burn cut off from each other.
questions: Can a Federation this fragmented actually be rebuilt one world at a time?
What is Book's place on a Starfleet ship, now that he is Burnham's partner as well as her civilian ally?
What crisis could possibly be big enough to interrupt the rebuild?

characters.name: Michael Burnham
characters.line: New captain of Discovery; spent a year alone in the 32nd century before her crew arrived, and it changed her.

characters.name: Cleveland Booker
characters.line: Former courier and empath known as Book; Burnham's partner and now a semi-official member of Discovery's crew.
characters.note: The friend and colleague of Book from S3 onward.

characters.name: Saru
characters.line: Former captain of Discovery, staying behind on Kaminar to raise the traumatised Kelpien child Su'Kal.

characters.name: Paul Stamets
characters.line: Chief engineer; still the only reliable human pilot of the spore drive.

characters.name: Hugh Culber
characters.line: Chief medical officer; one of the crew's emotional anchors as they adjust to the new century.

characters.name: Sylvia Tilly
characters.line: Bridge officer who briefly served as Saru's acting first officer during the season.

characters.name: Adira Tal
characters.line: Young human host of a Trill symbiont carrying the memories of a Federation admiral; now a member of Discovery's crew.

characters.name: Gray
characters.line: Adira's dead boyfriend, whose consciousness rides along inside them; visible only to Adira.

characters.name: Charles Vance
characters.line: Commander-in-Chief of what remains of Starfleet; cautious ally of Discovery who has come around to trusting them.

beats.label: S4 · Kwejian erased
beats.text: A mysterious gravitational anomaly obliterates Book's homeworld Kwejian, killing his brother and nephew. Book survives only because he was off-world when it hit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Book's grief-driven arc for the entire season and gives the DMA its first, personal cost.

beats.label: S4 · President Rillak
beats.text: New Federation president Laira Rillak leans on Captain Burnham while their teams pin the DMA on an unknown Species 10-C beyond the galactic barrier.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's antagonist, establishes Rillak as the political counterweight to Burnham, and points the show past the galactic barrier.

beats.label: S4 · Tarka's weapon
beats.text: Scientist Ruon Tarka builds a bomb to destroy the DMA. When the Federation votes for diplomacy instead, Tarka steals the weapon and Book, still grieving, joins him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits Book from Burnham and turns the season into a chase — the emotional crisis that carries the rest of it.

beats.label: S4 · Past the galactic barrier
beats.text: Discovery flies through the galactic barrier with Federation diplomats to attempt first contact with 10-C, while the DMA closes on Earth. Book and Tarka follow behind.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Burnham's mission and Book's mutiny on the same trajectory for the season's endgame.

beats.label: S4 · Speaking to 10-C
beats.text: Using a hydrocarbon-based language, the crew make contact with the hive-minded 10-C, who did not know the DMA was harming inhabited worlds. Talks begin to end it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes that the DMA is fixable by conversation — which is exactly what Tarka's plan is about to destroy.

beats.label: S4 · Tarka goes rogue
beats.text: Tarka pushes his plan anyway, sabotaging the talks and firing on the power source. General Ndoye rams Book's ship with a shuttle to stop him; Book is presumed dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Climactic cost of Book's grief and the moment the season's threads collide.

beats.label: S4 · A larger Federation
beats.text: The 10-C shut down the DMA and return Book alive. Earth rejoins the Federation, and Book accepts a sentence of helping the DMA's victims as reparation for his mutiny.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resets the board for next season: Federation growing, Burnham confirmed as its instrument, Book alive but at arm's length.

cliffhanger.text: The DMA is gone, Earth has rejoined the Federation, and Species 10-C are learning to atone. Burnham and her crew are stronger than ever; Book, still Kwejian's last survivor, is serving a sentence far from her side.
questions: Where do Burnham and Book stand while he serves his sentence away from Discovery?
What will the quietly influential Dr. Kovich ask Discovery to do next?
Now that a civilisation beyond the galaxy has been contacted, what other secrets is the 32nd century holding?

characters.name: Michael Burnham
characters.line: Captain of Discovery; tested hard by the DMA crisis and confirmed in her command.

characters.name: Cleveland Booker
characters.line: Last survivor of Kwejian; mutinied against the Federation out of grief and is now serving a sentence helping other DMA victims.

characters.name: Saru
characters.line: Returned to Discovery as Burnham's first officer; quietly courting Ni'Var president T'Rina.

characters.name: Paul Stamets
characters.line: Spore-drive engineer; took Book into the network for the flight beyond the galactic barrier.

characters.name: Hugh Culber
characters.line: Chief medical officer; more comfortable playing counsellor to the crew than he was on arrival in this century.

characters.name: Adira Tal
characters.line: Young Trill host, now a settled member of the bridge crew.

characters.name: Laira Rillak
characters.line: New Federation president; began by pushing hard on Burnham and ended the season working alongside her.

characters.name: T'Rina
characters.line: President of Ni'Var; Saru's fiancée.

characters.name: Dr. Kovich
characters.line: Enigmatic Federation intelligence figure who quietly steers Starfleet's biggest decisions from the wings.

beats.label: S5 · The Progenitors' technology
beats.text: Dr. Kovich sets Burnham on a red directive: find the ancient device the Progenitors used to seed life across the galaxy. Couriers Moll and L'ak grab the first clue.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's prize and its two antagonists in one beat.

beats.label: S5 · Rayner
beats.text: Captain Rayner nearly buries a town chasing Moll and is forced out of command. Burnham takes him on as first officer just as Saru leaves to marry Ni'Var's president T'Rina.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Installs the new first officer for the rest of the season and moves Saru out of the chair without killing him off.

beats.label: S5 · The trail of clues
beats.text: The crew race Moll across a Trill wilderness, a Mirror Universe Enterprise, and a pre-warp weather tower, gathering pieces of the map to the Progenitors' device.
beats.whyLoadBearing: One beat for the season's mid-run chase; none of the individual stops matter to later seasons, but the fact that Moll keeps up does.

beats.label: S5 · L'ak dies, Breen war
beats.text: L'ak, secretly Breen royalty, dies in Federation custody. Moll pledges to his people that the device will resurrect him, and Breen Primarch Ruhn declares war on the Federation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns a two-hander pursuit into a Federation-scale war and gives Moll the singular motive she carries into the finale.

beats.label: S5 · Moll takes command
beats.text: At the archive holding the last map piece, Moll kills Primarch Ruhn and takes his forces for herself. She and the Breen race Discovery to the Progenitors' hidden device.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Elevates Moll from courier to warlord — a live antagonist whose story is not finished.

beats.label: S5 · Nothing there for Moll
beats.text: Burnham reaches the device and meets a Progenitor, who confirms it cannot bring back the dead. Deciding no one should hold this power, Burnham drops it into a black hole.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the season's central quest and delivers Burnham's defining decision as captain.

beats.label: S5 · Years later
beats.text: Saru and T'Rina marry; Kovich is unmasked as time-agent Daniels. Years later, Admiral Burnham parks a restored Discovery at coordinates where Zora will wait for its next mission.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Time-jump epilogue that closes every open personal thread and parks the ship in place, whatever comes next.

cliffhanger.text: The Progenitors' technology is at the bottom of a black hole. Saru has married and left, Rayner runs the bridge, and years later Admiral Burnham has parked a restored Discovery at unnamed coordinates for a mission Zora will not attempt for a very long time.
questions: What mission is Zora waiting to carry out on Discovery's behalf?
What job does Kovich, now unmasked as time-agent Daniels, plan to offer Moll?
Who will command Discovery when its long wait is finally over?

characters.name: Michael Burnham
characters.line: Captain of Discovery during the search for the Progenitors' technology; an admiral by the season's epilogue.

characters.name: Cleveland Booker
characters.line: Burnham's partner, working his way back into Starfleet's trust after last season's mutiny.

characters.name: Rayner
characters.line: Discovery's new first officer; a hard-edged Kellerun and the survivor of a Breen occupation that killed his family.

characters.name: Saru
characters.line: Leaves Discovery to become a Federation ambassador and marries T'Rina by the season's end.

characters.name: Paul Stamets
characters.line: Spore-drive engineer; still the person the ship's most impossible manoeuvres run through.

characters.name: Hugh Culber
characters.line: Chief medical officer; spiritually shaken after briefly sharing his body with a Trill symbiont.

characters.name: T'Rina
characters.line: President of Ni'Var; marries Saru at the season's end.

characters.name: Moll
characters.line: Hardened courier who becomes leader of the Breen after killing Primarch Ruhn; escaped with her lover L'ak's body still in a pattern buffer.

characters.name: Dr. Kovich
characters.line: The mysterious Federation intelligence figure, revealed at last to be Agent Daniels — a time-travel operative from Starfleet's future.
